title: Trace calculus for finite-potent linear endomorphisms
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $V$ a $k$-vector space, of arbitrary dimension. Finite-dimensionality is as in [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and ordinary trace as in [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. Call $T\in\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ finite-potent if $T^N(V)$ is finite-dimensional for some $N\ge1$. There exists a canonical scalar $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(T)$: whenever $U\subset V$ is finite-dimensional, $T(U)\subset U$ and $T^N(V)\subset U$, it equals $\operatorname{Tr}_k(T|_U)$, independently of $U,N$. It agrees with ordinary trace when $V$ is finite-dimensional and is zero for a nilpotent endomorphism. For every $T$-stable subspace $L\subset V$, the restriction $T|_L$ and the induced map $\overline T$ on $V/L$ are finite-potent and
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},L}(T|_L)+\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V/L}(\overline T).$$
For $c\in k$, $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(cT)=c\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$. If $a:V\to W$, $b:W\to V$ are $k$-linear and $ba$ is finite-potent, then $ab$ is finite-potent and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},V}(ba)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp},W}(ab)$. Finally, if $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ are endomorphisms of $V$ such that every $T_iT_j$ has finite-dimensional image, then all $T_i$ and $\sum_i T_i$ are finite-potent and
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}\left(\sum_iT_i\right)=\sum_i\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T_i).$$

source.place: §1, pp. 149–150, T1–T5; T4 specialized to pairwise products of finite rank
